statement: What are the last two digits of $7^{2026}$?

choices.misconception: I only tracked the last digit, 9, and assumed the tens digit would be 0.
I noticed that $7^4 = 2401$ ends in 01 and assumed every large power of 7 ends in 01.
I listed the cycle 01, 07, 49, 43 starting from $7^0$ and took its second entry because 2026 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4.
I counted the powers left over after $7^{2024}$ as three instead of two.

hints: Work out the last two digits of the first few powers of 7.
Only the last two digits matter when you keep multiplying by 7. Look for a power of 7 whose last two digits are 01; after that the pattern of last two digits repeats.
$7^4 = 2401$ ends in 01, so the last two digits repeat every 4 powers: 07, 49, 43, 01.

solutions.reliable: The last two digits of $7^1, 7^2, 7^3, 7^4$ are 07, 49, 43, 01. Since $7^4$ ends in 01, multiplying by $7^4$ does not change the last two digits, so they repeat every 4 powers. As $2026 = 4 \times 506 + 2$, $7^{2026}$ ends in the same two digits as $7^2 = 49$. The transferable idea: a power ending in 01 makes the last two digits cycle.
solutions.elegant: $7^{2026} = (7^4)^{506} \times 7^2 = 2401^{506} \times 49$. Every power of 2401 ends in 01, and a number ending in 01 times 49 ends in 49. The transferable idea: split the exponent around a power that ends in 01.

whyOnTest: Last-digit cycles extend to the last two digits once you find a power ending in 01; the trap is tracking only the final digit.
